summary:
Long-duration spaceflight exposes astronauts to critical health risks like bone density loss and kidney stones, which are often diagnosed only after they become mission-threatening emergencies. Currently, tracking these interconnected issues requires time-consuming procedures that strain the crew's schedule.
Our solution is OrbitCare, an advanced predictive health monitoring software designed for maximum efficiency. OrbitCare transforms qualitative daily self-assessments—completed in under 60 seconds on a tablet—into quantitative, forecasted risk scores.

By analyzing the critical biological loops between bone loss, calcium excretion, spinal elongation, and reproductive health, our XGBoost machine learning engine calculates personalized risk profiles across three timelines: Current, Tomorrow, and Near Future. The software doesn’t just display data; its explainable AI identifies the root causes of elevated risks and instantly generates actionable countermeasures, such as automated hydration protocols or targeted resistive exercises.

Because real astronaut medical records are restricted, we validated our architecture using synthetic analog datasets built on robust clinical parameters. OrbitCare empowers astronauts to manage their health proactively and autonomously, mitigating serious medical events before they happen.
details:
How OrbitCare Works

OrbitCare operates as a highly efficient, closed-loop predictive health system. Astronauts interact with a minimalist UI to complete a daily 60-second digital assessment covering 38 critical biomarkers and subjective health indicators (e.g., hydration levels, pain scales, reproductive cycle data).

Behind the interface, an XGBoost Multi-Output Regressor processes these inputs. Instead of waiting for a threshold alert, the model maps the non-linear biological relationships and outputs a personalized Risk Percentage (0–100%) across three time horizons: Now, Tomorrow, and Near Future (3-months).
If a high risk is detected, our Explainable AI (Root Cause Analysis engine) extracts feature importances to tell the astronaut why the score is high (e.g., "85% Kidney Stone Risk due to high calcium excretion combined with low hydration"), and instantly triggers an actionable medical countermeasure.

Project Benefits

  • Extreme Time Efficiency: Replaces hours of cumbersome medical tracking with a sub-minute daily questionnaire.
  • Proactive vs. Reactive: Identifies the statistical trajectory of a kidney stone or spinal elongation pain days or weeks before it becomes physically debilitating.
  • Explainable AI Transparency: Doctors and astronauts require transparency. The system does not act as a "black box"; it justifies every high-risk score with concrete biological drivers.
  • Automated Countermeasures: Immediately translates predictive analytics into actionable steps, such as initiating targeted resistive exercises or adjusting fluid intake protocols.

Intended Impact

The primary impact of OrbitCare is enabling crew autonomy. As NASA looks toward Mars and deep-space Artemis missions, communication delays of up to 20 minutes make real-time telemedicine with Earth-bound flight surgeons impossible. OrbitCare empowers astronauts to independently monitor, forecast, and correct their own physiological degradation in microgravity, preventing mission-critical medical emergencies.
Tools, Languages, and Technologies

  • Machine Learning & Data Processing: Python, XGBoost, Scikit-learn (MultiOutputRegressor), Pandas, NumPy.
  • Development Environments: VS Code, Google Colab / Jupyter Notebooks, Python virtual environments.
  • Deployment & Backend: Flask/FastAPI (for the prediction endpoints) and Joblib for model serialization.
  • Frontend UI: HTML/CSS/JavaScript with responsive, space-friendly dark mode vectors and dynamic status charting.

Creativity and Innovation

Our core innovation is modeling the Calcium-Hormone Loop rather than treating health conditions in silos. Bone loss, kidney stones, and women's reproductive health are deeply intertwined in microgravity. Disruptions in menstrual cycles impact estrogen, which accelerates bone density loss, which dumps calcium into the urinary tract, which heavily spikes the risk of kidney stones.

By utilizing a Multi-Output Regression architecture, our AI maps these hidden, non-linear relationships across interconnected bodily systems simultaneously—something traditional linear monitoring software cannot do.

Key Factors Considered

  1. Astronaut Time Constraints: We heavily prioritized UI minimalism. Complex image-classification (CNN) workflows for daily scans were deemed too time-intensive for the crew. We pivoted to high-impact biomarker questionnaires that yield similar predictive value with zero setup time.
  2. Data Privacy Restrictions: Because real NASA Lifetime Surveillance of Astronaut Health (LSAH) data is restricted by HIPAA, we engineered a robust Python-based synthetic data generator. This allowed us to train and validate our XGBoost architecture using mathematically sound, clinical analog data without violating privacy laws.
  3. The "Black Box" Problem: We recognized that medical professionals will not trust a blind percentage. We intentionally engineered the system to extract and display Feature Importance, ensuring the AI is always clinically explainable.
